title: Etale direct-image finiteness over quasi-excellent bases
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $B$ be a finite field of characteristic $\ell$, and let $g:V\to T$ be a morphism of finite presentation between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume either that $g$ is proper, or that $T$ is quasi-excellent and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. Here quasi-excellent means that every affine open has a quasi-excellent coordinate ring [def-exc-excellent-ring]. On the ordinary small etale sites, let $Rg_*$ be derived direct image of sheaves of modules over the constant sheaves $B_V,B_T$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. In either case, for every bounded constructible complex $K$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], $Rg_*K$ is bounded constructible. If $g$ is proper, there is moreover an integer $d\geq0$ such that $R^qg_*M=0$ for every sheaf $M$ of $B_V$-modules and every $q>d$; this bound is independent of $M$, and the proper case requires neither a ground field nor quasi-excellence nor the invertibility of $\ell$. No bound uniform in $M$ is asserted in the nonproper case.

source.place: Theorem 6.7.1 (Grothendieck, Gabber), printed p.55, with complete Noetherian local ring R=B and maximal ideal zero; the cohomological-dimension clause is kept only for proper g, since for the quasi-excellent alternative Illusie-Laszlo-Orgogozo (literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf), Introduction Theorem 1 and Expose XIII Theorem 1.1.1, give constructibility with a vanishing bound depending on the constructible sheaf, and a uniform bound only for finite-dimensional bases

proof.text: First suppose $g$ is proper. Since it is of finite presentation it is of finite type, and $T$ is quasi-compact. Choose $e\geq0$ bounding the dimensions of all scheme-theoretic fibres by [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound]. The underlying abelian sheaf of any $B_V$-module $M$ is killed by $\ell$. Apply [lem-kun-proper-torsion-cd-bound] to this sheaf. The comparison [lem-sbc-higher-direct-image-forget-comparison] identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of $R^qg_*M$ with that higher direct image. Consequently $R^qg_*M=0$ for $q>2e$. Take $d=2e$. This proves the requested uniform bound, without imposing any condition on the characteristic of the residue fields or on the base beyond those already stated.

source.place: Tag 095U, label lemma-cohomological-dimension-proper; morphisms.tex Tag 0A3V, label lemma-morphism-finite-type-bounded-dimension

proof.text: For the same proper $g$ and a constructible sheaf $M$ in degree zero, apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-compactification-constructibility] to the identity compactification $V\xrightarrow{1}V\xrightarrow{g}T$. The identity is a quasi-compact open immersion; $g$ is separated and of finite presentation, and both schemes are qcqs, as that node requires. Its output is $Rg_*M$ by [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], so every cohomology sheaf is constructible. The nonnegative injective resolution computing right-derived direct image has no negative cohomology. Step 1 kills degrees above $2e$; hence $Rg_*M$ is bounded constructible.

source.place: Tag 0GL0, label theorem-constructible-shriek, applied to the identity compactification

proof.text: We will use the following finite devissage for any of the direct images in this proof. Bounded constructible complexes are closed under shifts and distinguished triangles: the long exact cohomology sequence expresses each middle cohomology as an extension of a cokernel and a kernel of the adjacent maps, which are constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]; the union of finitely many degree intervals is bounded. Right-derived direct image preserves distinguished triangles and shifts by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. If it sends each constructible sheaf to a bounded constructible complex, it therefore does the same for every bounded constructible $K$: induct on the length of a cohomological interval $[a,b]$ using [lem-sf-derived-truncation-triangle] at $b$, whose terms are $\tau_{\leq b-1}K$ and $\mathcal H^b(K)[-b]$. The zero case is immediate; the two shorter terms give the induction step. This applies Step 2 to the proper case. It also shows that subsequent sheaf finiteness inputs need no bound uniform over all constructible sheaves.

source.place: Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle; finite devissage as in ILO XIII, 1.1.2

proof.text: Now suppose $T$ is quasi-excellent and $\ell$ is invertible on $T$. The stability lemma [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] applied to $1_T$ and to $g$ shows that $T$ and $V$ are Noetherian. For any Noetherian quasi-excellent $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible and any open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, [lem-per-gabber-open-immersion-sheaf-finiteness] gives constructible cohomology and an eventual-vanishing bound for $Rj_*M$ for every constructible $M$. Its negative degrees vanish by the bounded-below resolution definition [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Thus Step 3 gives $Rj_*D^b_c(U,B)\subset D^b_c(W,B)$. No finite-dimensionality of $W$ is used.

Consider first a separated finite-type morphism $h:Z\to W$ with $W$ Noetherian quasi-excellent, $\ell$ invertible on $W$, and $Z$ qcqs. By [thm-nagata-compactification] choose $Z\xrightarrow{j}\overline Z\xrightarrow{p}W$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $p$ proper [def-nagata-compactification]. The stability lemma [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] applies to $p$: $\overline Z$ is quasi-excellent and Noetherian, since $p$ is of finite type and its source is quasi-compact. The element $\ell$ stays a unit on $\overline Z$ because a ring homomorphism carries an inverse to an inverse. By [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], $p$ is locally of finite presentation; properness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, hence quasi-separatedness, so $p$ is finitely presented and Steps 1--3 apply to it, while Step 4 applies to $j$. For $K\in D^b_c(Z,B)$ the composition isomorphism [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence] gives $Rh_*K\simeq Rp_*Rj_*K\in D^b_c(W,B)$.

source.place: XIII 2.1.2 and 3.1, reduction to an open immersion using a compactification

proof.text: To treat an arbitrary $g$ in the quasi-excellent case, first restrict to an affine open $W\subset T$. The module-coefficient restriction isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-open-restriction] identifies $(Rg_*K)|_W$ with $R(g_W)_*(K|_{V_W})$. The input remains bounded constructible: inverse-image restriction intersects each stratum with the open and restricts its local constant trivializations [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. The scheme $V_W$ is Noetherian by [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] and has a finite affine cover by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. For each member of this cover its map to the affine $W$ is separated: the diagonal of a morphism between affine schemes is the closed immersion defined on rings by the surjective multiplication map. Every open subscheme of such an affine member remains separated over $W$, since its relative diagonal is the restriction of that closed diagonal. For the overlap of a finite union of these affines with one more affine, [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc] gives quasi-compactness, using that $V_W$ is quasi-separated. Its inclusion into the affine member is then of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], so its map to $W$ is of finite type as well.

source.place: XIII 2.1.2, localization on the target and finite affine coverings of the source

proof.text:
Here is the relative two-open Mayer--Vietoris argument needed to glue the preceding separated cases. If $Z=U\cup U'$ and $h:Z\to W$, represent $L\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ by a bounded-below injective complex $I$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives], its restrictions to $U,U',U\cap U'$ remain injective complexes. Apply [lem-dg-etale-injective-finite-cech-rows] with the two-open cover in every degree: the augmented row is split exact. Applying $h_*$ preserves its splitting and gives a short exact sequence of complexes
$$0\to h_*I\to (h|_U)_*(I|_U)\oplus(h|_{U'})_*(I|_{U'})\to(h|_{U\cap U'})_*(I|_{U\cap U'})\to0.$$
By the injective-resolution computation [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] these are representatives of the corresponding derived images. Their cohomology long exact sequence, together with the kernel/cokernel/extension closure [thm-constructible-serre], implies that the first derived image is bounded constructible whenever the other three are: outside their finite degree intervals both neighbouring groups are zero; in each remaining degree the first group is an extension of a cokernel by a kernel.

source.place: Tag 0EYK, label lemma-relative-mayer-vietoris, proof, applied to constant-ring module injective complexes

proof.text: Induct on the number $r$ of affine opens in the chosen cover of $V_W$. If $r=0$, $V_W$ is empty and its image is zero. For $r=1$ the map is separated, so Step 5 applies. For $r>1$, let $U$ be the union of the first $r-1$ affine opens and $U'$ the last affine open. The image from $U$ is bounded constructible by induction. The images from $U'$ and $U\cap U'$ are bounded constructible by Step 5: by Step 6 the latter is a quasi-compact open of the affine $U'$, separated and of finite type over $W$. Step 7 proves bounded constructibility over $W$. Finally choose finitely many affine opens $W_i$ covering the quasi-compact $T$. The restrictions of $Rg_*K$ have finite cohomological intervals; their finite union gives a global interval. For each cohomology sheaf, the finitely many local finite stratifications give a global one: order all their locally closed constructible strata, subtract the previously occurring ones, and refine each remaining constructible difference into finitely many locally closed pieces using the Boolean-algebra and locally closed decomposition properties in [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Each piece lies inside an original stratum and retains its finite locally constant trivialization. Thus the global cohomology is constructible by [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. This proves the remaining case, with a bound allowed to depend on $K$.
